sanskrit: anyo duryodhanāt karṇāc chakuneś cāpi saubalāt duḥśāsanacaturthānāṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmi pañcamam
english: Apart from Duryodhana, from Karṇa, and from Śakuni the son of Subala, with Duḥśāsana as the fourth—I can see no fifth man among them.

sanskrit: yeṣām abhīśuhastaḥ syād viṣvakseno rathe sthitaḥ saṃnaddhaś cārjuno yoddhā teṣāṃ nāsti parājayaḥ
english: Those upon whose chariot Viṣvaksena stands with the reins in his hand, and who have Arjuna for their armored warrior—for them there is no defeat.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ mama vilāpānāṃ na hi duryodhanaḥ smaret hatau hi puruṣavyāghrau bhīṣmadroṇau tvam āttha me
english: Duryodhana would not remember these laments of mine. Now you tell me that the two tigers among men, Bhīṣma and Droṇa, are slain.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ viduravākyānām uktānāṃ dīrghadarśinām dṛṣṭvemāṃ phalanirvṛttiṃ manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing this ripening of the fruit of those far-seeing words once spoken by Vidura, I think my little sons now grieve.

sanskrit: himātyaye yathā kakṣaṃ śuṣkaṃ vāterito mahān agnir dahet tathā senāṃ māmikāṃ sa dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: As at winter's end a great fire, driven by the wind, burns up the dry brushwood, so does that Dhanaṃjaya consume my army.

sanskrit: ācakṣva tad dhi naḥ sarvaṃ kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya yad upāyāt tu sāyāhne kṛtvā pārthasya kilbiṣam abhimanyau hate tāta katham āsīn mano hi vaḥ
english: Tell us the whole of it, for you are skilled, Saṃjaya—what came about toward evening, the wrong done to Pārtha. When Abhimanyu was slain, my son, what then was the mood among you?

sanskrit: na jātu tasya karmāṇi yudhi gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ apakṛtvā mahat tāta soḍhuṃ śakṣyanti māmakāḥ
english: Never, my son, having done so great a wrong, will my people be able to withstand in battle the deeds of him who wields the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu duryodhanaḥ kṛtyaṃ karṇaḥ kṛtyaṃ kim abravīt duḥśāsanaḥ saubalaś ca teṣām evaṃ gate api sarveṣāṃ samavetānāṃ putrāṇāṃ mama saṃjaya
english: What did Duryodhana resolve to do? What did Karṇa, what did Duḥśāsana and the son of Subala say must be done, matters having gone thus, when all my sons were assembled together, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: yad vṛttaṃ tāta saṃgrāme mandasyāpanayair bhṛśam lobhānugatadurbuddheḥ krodhena vikṛtātmanaḥ
english: What came to pass in the battle, my son, through the grievous misdeeds of that dull-witted one—his mind warped by greed, his self deformed by wrath—

sanskrit: rājyakāmasya mūḍhasya rāgopahatacetasaḥ durnītaṃ vā sunītaṃ vā tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: of that fool who craves the kingdom, whose understanding is undone by passion—whether it was ill-counseled or well-counseled, that tell me, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hanta te saṃpravakṣyāmi sarvaṃ pratyakṣadarśivān śuśrūṣasva sthiro bhūtvā tava hy apanayo mahān
english: Saṃjaya said: Come then, I shall relate it all to you, for I saw it with my own eyes. Listen, and be steadfast—for great indeed is the misdeed that is yours.

sanskrit: gatodake setubandho yādṛk tādṛg ayaṃ tava vilāpo niṣphalo rājan mā śuco bharatarṣabha
english: As the building of a dam once the water has run off, such is this lament of yours—fruitless, O king. Grieve not, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: anatikramaṇīyo 'yaṃ kṛtāntasyādbhuto vidhiḥ mā śuco bharataśreṣṭha diṣṭam etat purātanam
english: This wondrous ordinance of Fate is not to be overstepped. Grieve not, O best of the Bharatas—this was destined from of old.

sanskrit: yadi hi tvaṃ purā dyūtāt kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram nivartayethāḥ putrāṃś ca na tvāṃ vyasanam āvrajet
english: Had you of old turned Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī, and your own sons, back from the dicing, this calamity would not have come upon you.

sanskrit: yuddhakāle punaḥ prāpte tadaiva bhavatā yadi nivartitāḥ syuḥ saṃrabdhā na tvāṃ vyasanam āvrajet
english: And again, when the time of war had come, had you even then turned back those who were inflamed, this calamity would not have come upon you.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ cāvidheyaṃ badhnīteti purā yadi kurūn acodayiṣyas tvaṃ na tvāṃ vyasanam āvrajet
english: And had you of old urged the Kurus, saying, 'Bind this unruly Duryodhana,' this calamity would not have come upon you.

sanskrit: tat te buddhivyabhīcāram upalapsyanti pāṇḍavāḥ pāñcālā vṛṣṇayaḥ sarve ye cānye 'pi mahājanāḥ
english: This straying of your judgment the Pāṇḍavas will mark, and the Pāñcālas, and the Vṛṣṇis, and all the other great folk besides.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā pitṛkarma tvaṃ putraṃ saṃsthāpya satpathe vartethā yadi dharmeṇa na tvāṃ vyasanam āvrajet
english: Had you, doing a father's duty and setting your son upon the good path, conducted yourself according to dharma, this calamity would not have come upon you.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu prājñatamo loke hitvā dharmaṃ sanātanam duryodhanasya karṇasya śakuneś cānvagā matam
english: But you, wisest of men in the world, forsaking the eternal dharma, followed the counsel of Duryodhana, of Karṇa, and of Śakuni.

sanskrit: tat te vilapitaṃ sarvaṃ mayā rājan niśāmitam arthe niviśamānasya viṣamiśraṃ yathā madhu
english: All this lament of yours I have heard, O king—the lament of one who clings to his gain, like honey laced with poison.

sanskrit: na tathā manyate kṛṣṇo rājānaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ purā na bhīṣmaṃ naiva ca droṇaṃ yathā tvāṃ manyate nṛpa
english: Kṛṣṇa does not so esteem King Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava of old, nor Bhīṣma, nor even Droṇa, as he esteems you, O king.

sanskrit: vyajānata yadā tu tvāṃ rājadharmād adhaś cyutam tadā prabhṛti kṛṣṇas tvāṃ na tathā bahu manyate
english: But from the moment he understood you to have fallen away from the king's duty, from then on Kṛṣṇa no longer holds you in such high regard.

sanskrit: paruṣāṇy ucyamānāṃś ca yathā pārthān upekṣase tasyānubandhaḥ prāptas tvāṃ putrāṇāṃ rājyakāmukam
english: And because you looked on indifferently while the sons of Pṛthā were addressed with harsh words, the consequence of that has overtaken you, who craved the kingdom for your sons.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyam apavṛttaṃ tadānagha atha pārthair jitāṃ kṛtsnāṃ pṛthivīṃ pratyapadyathāḥ
english: The kingdom of your fathers and forefathers had then passed away from you, O blameless one; yet through the Pārthas you regained the whole earth they had conquered.

sanskrit: pāṇḍunāvarjitaṃ rājyaṃ kauravāṇāṃ yaśas tathā tataś cābhyadhikaṃ bhūyaḥ pāṇḍavair dharmacāribhiḥ
english: The kingdom won by Pāṇḍu, and the glory of the Kauravas—the Pāṇḍavas, walkers in dharma, made it yet greater than before.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tat tādṛśaṃ karma tvām āsādya suniṣphalam yat pitryād bhraṃśitā rājyāt tvayehāmiṣagṛddhinā
english: That great work of theirs, coming to you, was rendered wholly fruitless, for by you, greedy for the spoil, they were cast out of their ancestral kingdom.

sanskrit: yat punar yuddhakāle tvaṃ putrān garhayase nṛpa bahudhā vyāharan doṣān na tad adyopapadyate
english: That now, in the time of war, you reproach your sons, O king, recounting their faults in many ways—this is not fitting today.

sanskrit: na hi rakṣanti rājāno yudhyanto jīvitaṃ raṇe camūṃ vigāhya pārthānāṃ yudhyante kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: For kings who fight do not guard their lives in battle; plunging into the host of the Pārthas, those bulls among kṣatriyas do battle.

sanskrit: yāṃ tu kṛṣṇārjunau senāṃ yāṃ sātyakivṛkodarau rakṣeran ko nu tāṃ yudhyec camūm anyatra kauravaiḥ
english: That army which Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, which Sātyaki and Vṛkodara guard—who could give battle to such a host, save the Kauravas?

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ yoddhā guḍākeśo yeṣāṃ mantrī janārdanaḥ yeṣāṃ ca sātyakir goptā yeṣāṃ goptā vṛkodaraḥ
english: They whose warrior is Guḍākeśa, whose counselor is Janārdana, whose protector is Sātyaki, whose protector is Vṛkodara—

sanskrit: ko hi tān viṣahed yoddhuṃ martyadharmā dhanurdharaḥ anyatra kauraveyebhyo ye vā teṣāṃ padānugāḥ
english: what bowman of mortal nature could endure to fight them, save the Kauravas and those who follow in their train?

sanskrit: yāvat tu śakyate kartum anuraktair janādhipaiḥ kṣatradharmarataiḥ śūrais tāvat kurvanti kauravāḥ
english: As much as can be done by devoted kings, by heroes given to the duty of the warrior caste, so much the Kauravas are doing.

sanskrit: yathā tu puruṣavyāghrair yuddhaṃ paramasaṅkaṭam kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ tat sarvaṃ śṛṇu tattvataḥ
english: Now how that most terrible battle of the Kurus, those tigers among men, was waged together with the Pāṇḍavas—hear it all in truth.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasyāṃ niśāyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ svāny anīkāni sarvāṇi prākrāmad vyūhituṃ tataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When that night had passed into dawn, Droṇa, best of those who bear arms, set about marshaling all his own divisions into array.

sanskrit: śūrāṇāṃ garjatāṃ rājan saṃkruddhānām amarṣiṇām śrūyante sma giraś citrāḥ parasparavadhaiṣiṇām
english: From the roaring heroes, O king—wrathful, unforgiving, each seeking the other's death—were heard manifold cries.

sanskrit: visphārya ca dhanūṃṣy ājau jyāḥ karaiḥ parimṛjya ca viniḥśvasantaḥ prākrośan kvedānīṃ sa dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Twanging their bows in the fray and stroking the bowstrings with their hands, breathing hard, they cried aloud, 'Where now is that Dhanaṃjaya?'

sanskrit: vikośān sutsarūn anye kṛtadhārān samāhitān pītān ākāśasaṃkāśān asīn ke cic ca cikṣipuḥ
english: And some flung up their swords—unsheathed, fair-hilted, well-whetted, well-tempered, polished, gleaming like the sky.

sanskrit: carantas tv asimārgāṃś ca dhanurmārgāṃś ca śikṣayā saṃgrāmamanasaḥ śūrā dṛśyante sma sahasraśaḥ
english: Practicing the ways of the sword and the ways of the bow with skill, heroes whose minds were set on battle were seen there by the thousand.

sanskrit: saghaṇṭāś candanādigdhāḥ svarṇavajravibhūṣitāḥ samutkṣipya gadāś cānye paryapṛcchanta pāṇḍavam
english: And others, hung with bells, smeared with sandal, adorned with gold and diamond, raising up their maces, kept asking after the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: anye balamadonmattāḥ parighair bāhuśālinaḥ cakruḥ saṃbādham ākāśam ucchritendradhvajopamaiḥ
english: Others, drunk with the pride of strength, mighty of arm, crowded the very sky with their iron clubs, like upraised banners of Indra.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇaiś cānye vicitrasragalaṃkṛtāḥ saṃgrāmamanasaḥ śūrās tatra tatra vyavasthitāḥ
english: And others, bearing weapons of every kind, decked with garlands of varied hue, heroes whose minds were set on battle, took their stations here and there.

sanskrit: kvārjunaḥ kva ca govindaḥ kva ca mānī vṛkodaraḥ kva ca te suhṛdas teṣām āhvayanto raṇe tadā
english: 'Where is Arjuna? Where Govinda? Where the proud Vṛkodara? Where are those friends of theirs?'—so they called out then in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkham upādhmāya tvarayan vājinaḥ svayam itas tatas tān racayan droṇaś carati vegitaḥ
english: Then Droṇa, having blown his conch and himself urging on his horses, ranging here and there to set them in order, moved about at speed.

sanskrit: teṣv anīkeṣu sarveṣu sthiteṣv āhavanandiṣu bhāradvājo mahārāja jayadratham athābravīt
english: When all those divisions, rejoicing in battle, stood in their places, the son of Bharadvāja, O great king, then spoke to Jayadratha:

sanskrit: tvaṃ caiva saumadattiś ca karṇaś caiva mahārathaḥ aśvatthāmā ca śalyaś ca vṛṣasenaḥ kṛpas tathā
english: 'You, and the son of Somadatta, and Karṇa the great chariot-warrior, and Aśvatthāman, and Śalya, and Vṛṣasena, and Kṛpa as well—'

sanskrit: śataṃ cāśvasahasrāṇāṃ rathānām ayutāni ṣaṭ dviradānāṃ prabhinnānāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: 'a hundred thousand horse, sixty thousand chariots, fourteen thousand rutting elephants in their must,'

sanskrit: padātīnāṃ sahasrāṇi daṃśitāny ekaviṃśatiḥ gavyūtiṣu trimātreṣu mām anāsādya tiṣṭhata
english: 'and one-and-twenty thousand mailed foot-soldiers—take your stand at a distance of three leagues from me, without coming near.'

sanskrit: tatrasthaṃ tvāṃ na saṃsoḍhuṃ śaktā devāḥ savāsavāḥ kiṃ punaḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve samāśvasihi saindhava
english: 'Standing there, not even the gods with Vāsava could prevail against you—how much less all the Pāṇḍavas. Take heart, O lord of the Sindhus.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ samāśvastaḥ sindhurājo jayadrathaḥ saṃprāyāt saha gāndhārair vṛtas taiś ca mahārathaiḥ varmibhiḥ sādibhir yattaiḥ prāsapāṇibhir āsthitaiḥ
english: So addressed and reassured, Jayadratha the king of the Sindhus set forth with the Gāndhāras, surrounded by those great chariot-warriors, by mailed riders ready and resolute, lances in hand.

sanskrit: cāmarāpīḍinaḥ sarve jāmbūnadavibhūṣitāḥ jayadrathasya rājendra hayāḥ sādhupravāhinaḥ te caiva saptasāhasrā dvisāhasrāś ca saindhavāḥ
english: All crowned with yak-tail plumes and adorned with the gold of the Jambū river, the horses of Jayadratha, O lord of kings, ran true and well—seven thousand of them, and two thousand Sindhu steeds besides.

sanskrit: mattānām adhirūḍhānāṃ hastyārohair viśāradaiḥ nāgānāṃ bhīmarūpāṇāṃ varmiṇāṃ raudrakarmiṇām
english: Of must-maddened elephants, mounted by skilled drivers—great beasts of terrible shape, armored, of dreadful deeds—

sanskrit: adhyardhena sahasreṇa putro durmarṣaṇas tava agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ yotsyamāno vyavasthitaḥ
english: with fifteen hundred of these your son Durmarṣaṇa took his stand at the head of all the armies, ready to fight.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsanaś caiva vikarṇaś ca tavātmajau sindhurājārthasiddhyartham agrānīke vyavasthitau
english: Then Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa, those sons of yours, for the accomplishing of the Sindhu king's purpose, took their places in the foremost division.

sanskrit: dīrgho dvādaśagavyūtiḥ paścārdhe pañca vistṛtaḥ vyūhaḥ sa cakraśakaṭo bhāradvājena nirmitaḥ
english: Twelve leagues long, and in its rear half five leagues broad, that 'wheel-and-cart' array was fashioned by the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: nānānṛpatibhir vīrais tatra tatra vyavasthitaiḥ rathāśvagajapattyoghair droṇena vihitaḥ svayam
english: With sundry heroic kings stationed here and there, with floods of chariots, horse, elephants, and foot, it was disposed by Droṇa himself.

sanskrit: paścārdhe tasya padmas tu garbhavyūhaḥ sudurbhidaḥ sūcī padmasya madhyastho gūḍho vyūhaḥ punaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: In its rear half was a lotus, an inner array hard to break through; and within the heart of the lotus a needle-formation, a hidden array, was again contrived.

sanskrit: evam etaṃ mahāvyūhaṃ vyūhya droṇo vyavasthitaḥ sūcīmukhe maheṣvāsaḥ kṛtavarmā vyavasthitaḥ
english: Having marshaled this great array thus, Droṇa took his stand; and at the mouth of the needle the great archer Kṛtavarman was posted.

sanskrit: anantaraṃ ca kāmbojo jalasaṃdhaś ca māriṣa duryodhanaḥ sahāmātyas tadanantaram eva ca
english: Next to him the Kāmboja and Jalasaṃdha, O sire; and immediately after them Duryodhana together with his counselors.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṇi yodhānām anivartinām vyavasthitāni sarvāṇi śakaṭe sūcirakṣiṇaḥ
english: Then hundreds of thousands of warriors who would never turn back were all stationed in the cart-array, guarding the needle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ca pṛṣṭhato rāja balena mahatā vṛtaḥ jayadrathas tato rājan sūcipāśe vyavasthitaḥ
english: And behind them, O king, encompassed by a great force, Jayadratha then took his stand at the noose of the needle.

sanskrit: śakaṭasya tu rājendra bhāradvājo mukhe sthitaḥ anu tasyābhavad bhojo jugopainaṃ tataḥ svayam
english: At the mouth of the cart, O lord of kings, stood the son of Bharadvāja; behind him was the Bhoja, who then guarded him himself.

sanskrit: śvetavarmāmbaroṣṇīṣo vyūḍhorasko mahābhujaḥ dhanur visphārayan droṇas tasthau kruddha ivāntakaḥ
english: In white armor, white robe, and white turban, broad-chested and mighty-armed, twanging his bow, Droṇa stood like the wrathful Ender of all.

sanskrit: patākinaṃ śoṇahayaṃ vedīkṛṣṇājinadhvajam droṇasya ratham ālokya prahṛṣṭāḥ kuravo 'bhavan
english: Beholding Droṇa's chariot—pennoned, drawn by red horses, bearing for its standard an altar and a black antelope-skin—the Kurus grew glad.

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇasaṃghānāṃ vismayaḥ sumahān abhūt droṇena vihitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyūhaṃ kṣubdhārṇavopamam
english: A very great wonder arose among the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas as they beheld the array disposed by Droṇa, like a heaving ocean.

sanskrit: saśailasāgaravanāṃ nānājanapadākulām grased vyūhaḥ kṣitiṃ sarvām iti bhūtāni menire
english: 'This array would swallow up the whole earth, with its mountains, seas, and forests, thronged with its many peoples'—so thought the living beings.

sanskrit: bahurathamanujāśvapattināgaṃ; pratibhayanisvanam adbhutābharūpam ahitahṛdayabhedanaṃ mahad vai; śakaṭam avekṣya kṛtaṃ nananda rājā
english: Thronged with many chariots, men, horses, foot, and elephants, of fearful clamor and wondrous shape, rending the hearts of foes—beholding that vast cart-array thus made, the king rejoiced.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu samutkruṣṭeṣu māriṣa tāḍyamānāsu bherīṣu mṛdaṅgeṣu nadatsu ca
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when the divisions had been marshaled and the war-cry raised, O sire, when the kettledrums were beaten and the tabors thundered,

sanskrit: anīkānāṃ ca saṃhrāde vāditrāṇāṃ ca nisvane pradhmāpiteṣu śaṅkheṣu saṃnāde lomaharṣaṇe
english: amid the roar of the armies and the din of instruments, when the conches were sounded and the uproar was such as made the hair stand on end—

sanskrit: abhihārayatsu śanakair bharateṣu yuyutsuṣu raudre muhūrte saṃprāpte savyasācī vyadṛśyata
english: as the Bharatas, eager for the fight, slowly advanced, and the dread hour came on, Savyasācin appeared.

sanskrit: vaḍānāṃ vāyasānāṃ ca purastāt savyasācinaḥ bahulāni sahasrāṇi prākrīḍaṃs tatra bhārata
english: Of herons and of crows, before Savyasācin, many thousands sported there, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: mṛgāś ca ghorasaṃnādāḥ śivāś cāśivadarśanāḥ dakṣiṇena prayātānām asmākaṃ prāṇadaṃs tathā
english: And beasts of dreadful cry, and jackals of ill-omened aspect, howled on the right hand of us as we marched forth.

sanskrit: sanirghātā jvalantyaś ca petur ulkāḥ samantataḥ cacāla ca mahī kṛtsnā bhaye ghore samutthite
english: Blazing meteors fell on every side with thunderous crashes, and the whole earth trembled as a dread terror arose.

sanskrit: viṣvag vātāḥ sanirghātā rūkṣāḥ śarkaravarṣiṇaḥ vavur āyāti kaunteye saṃgrāme samupasthite
english: Harsh winds raising thunderclaps and showering grit blew from every quarter as the son of Kuntī drew near and the battle was at hand.

sanskrit: nākulis tu śatānīko dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkāni prājñau tau vyūhatus tadā
english: Then Śatānīka the son of Nakula, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata—those two prudent ones—marshaled the divisions of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa dviradānāṃ śatena ca tribhir aśvasahasraiś ca padātīnāṃ śataiḥ śataiḥ
english: Then with a thousand chariots, a hundred elephants, three thousand horse, and hundreds upon hundreds of foot-soldiers,

sanskrit: adhyardhamātre dhanuṣāṃ sahasre tanayas tava agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ sthitvā durmarṣaṇo 'bravīt
english: with full fifteen hundred bows, your son Durmarṣaṇa, taking his stand at the head of all the armies, spoke thus:

sanskrit: adya gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ tapantaṃ yuddhadurmadam aham āvārayiṣyāmi veleva makarālayam
english: 'This day I will hold back the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, scorching and battle-mad, as the shore holds back the abode of the sea-monsters.'

sanskrit: adya paśyantu saṃgrāme dhanaṃjayam amarṣaṇam viṣaktaṃ mayi durdharṣam aśmakūṭam ivāśmani
english: 'This day let them behold in battle the unforgiving Dhanaṃjaya, hard to assail, fastened upon me as a hammer of stone upon a stone.'

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvan mahārāja mahātmā sa mahāmatiḥ maheṣvāsair vṛto rājan maheṣvāso vyavasthitaḥ
english: Speaking thus, O great king, that high-souled one of great mind, a mighty archer surrounded by mighty archers, took his stand, O king.

sanskrit: tato 'ntaka iva kruddhaḥ savajra iva vāsavaḥ daṇḍapāṇir ivāsahyo mṛtyuḥ kālena coditaḥ
english: Then, like the wrathful Ender, like Vāsava bearing the thunderbolt, unbearable as Yama rod in hand—like Death itself driven on by Time—
